question.text:
Consider the following $3$-address code sequence. This code is divided into basic blocks. How many basic blocks are there? (Answer as an integer)

 

1: a = 1
2: b = 2
3: if a > b goto 7
4: c = a + b
5: d = c *2
6: goto 8
7: c = a - b
8: a = c + 1
9: print a
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following $3$-address code sequence. This code is divided into basic blocks. How many basic blocks are there? (Answer as an integer)

 

1: i = 0
2: sum = 0
3: t1 = i < 10
4: if t1 == 0 goto 11
5: t2 = i * 4
6: t3 = arr[t2]
7: sum = sum + t3
8: i = i + 1
9: goto 3
10: goto 14
11: avg = sum / 10
12: print avg
13: goto 10
14: end

& \verb|2005: t2 = arr[t1]| \\
& \verb|2006: if t2 > y goto 2010| \\
& \verb|2007: x = x + t2| \\
& \verb|2008: i = i + 1| \\
& \verb|2009: if i <= 15 goto 2004| \\
& \verb|2010: y = y / 2| \\
